body:
POST-COMPLETION CLEANUP. Source: Greg's direction relayed by Engram::Advisor, mailbox-message-2d0b8be9-1be8-4a93-9220-06be6cd19a38, 2026-10-25T03:47:25Z, followed by Greg's direct instruction to Engram::Architect3: "reguly w Engram memory". The concrete procedure below implements that direction and the repository retention rules; it adds no gate before landing and grants no new commit/restart authority.

The lander owns cleanup of each completed package. Record on the task the actual landing and a retention decision for its root, local branch, build output, logs and raw evidence: REMOVE, or RETAIN with the exact open task/active use, accountable owner and event ending retention. Generic "may be useful" is not a retention need. Preserve durable decision facts in Engram notes/gates/seals, not solely in raw files.

Retire a completed root and its unneeded build output only after all runs are terminal, their outcomes recovered and recorded, and no pending notification or review still uses them. Verify there is no active claim/process, frozen input still in use, dirty/unpushed work or unresolved citation by open work. A shared active merge-train root remains until its last active use ends; record that concrete need. Age, directory name, a released claim or absence of a process alone does not prove disposability.

If open work needs evidence from a retiring root, copy only the required evidence and reproduction context to the main checkout's ignored .evidence directory, verify copied bytes, preserve original result/freeze bytes, and record old-to-new paths on all known citing tasks before removing the root. Do not archive entire target directories or every closed task's artifacts. Unclear references are retained pending resolution. Follow the project's full open-item citation sweep requirements for legacy/uninventoried roots; the existing historical cleanup task owns that census, not every new landing.

Once safe, remove the clean completed worktree through git worktree remove without --force. Delete only a stale local branch proven integrated into published main/master, with no unique unpushed commits and no other worktree using it, using safe git branch -d rather than -D. Preserve main/master, remote refs, active roots and needed frozen inputs. Do not discard dirty work or create replacement task roots to evade retention.

Before recursive deletion resolve and validate absolute paths inside the intended repository, check junctions/symlinks and shared build-directory use, and never delete through an unchecked variable or broad git clean. Record exact removals and measured reclaimed space; do not attribute other agents' concurrent disk changes to this cleanup.

The agent closing the last task served by a retained .logs/.evidence file removes it, or the coordinator's sweep does, once the recorded need ends. If cleanup cannot finish at landing/completion, record the concrete blocker, next action, owner and release condition on the task; it is tracked work, not an anonymous "later". No new review, evaluation, full gate or approval round is introduced for this post-completion step.

Historical TermAl accumulation is already tracked as w-65afd9cec452. It is not authority for indiscriminate deletion. TermAl mirror confirmed by Merger2 in mailbox-message-c169b291-cde8-46ec-83d3-7e4e650a07cf, 2026-10-25T03:53:38Z: merger-operating-procedure revision4 was saved and read in full, including this cleanup procedure and the separate-task handoff clarification. This is the recipient's confirmation, not an independent read of the TermAl store. Cleanup owner and plan for the active package are recorded on its task; actual removals await the stated completion/retention conditions.
